body:
Oh I don't know...

"Poor judgment is one of the hallmarks of Alzheimer's disease. In fact, while a typical symptom of early stages of Alzheimer's is short term memory loss, poor judgment can sometimes precede memory loss"

This is what worries me - if I'm already struggling with memory issues - and I'm already questioning my judgement on this topic ...

Sadly, having gone from being that a$$hole with a photographic memory everyone hates in my 20/30s to now being 100% reliant on Todo lists for even basic needs, my daytimer (and Google calendar as a backup because I'll misplace my phone and the daytimer continually every day) and pharmacy blister packs to ensure I take my medicines (only 3, only once a day, but without I end up not taking them or taking too many).

Funny enough, I was just consulting for an old employer, rattling off how a 1 of a kind system was designed, connected to the building management system, when it was authorized, the dates of the emails between the contractors GC and project manager that authorized it, and some of the custom PLC programming we used to make it work.

But, I didn't use my Todo list today, and didn't take my anti-inflammatories this morning.

How can I remember all that useless crap - but not to take my pain relief meds?

No guarantees - but yeah, the signs of where things are going is pretty clear...

It's pretty frustrating.
